💻 **→** Next: the EVA class definition and one sandboxed instance per job, starting with EVA-03 (owner, 2026-11-05).

|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner questions 2026-11-05: why one EVA-00, -01, -02 per machine, two copies of a pilot, two EVA-02 with two agents. Today no EVA exists: every action runs inside the scheduler process (the dashboard's "EVA-02 · in-process executor, not sandboxed yet"), and the four cage slots were a drawing, not a rule. |
| **Reproduce** | Look at the dashboard's EVA cages: three say planned, EVA-02 runs in process. |

### <a id="f-087"></a>[✨ F-087](#top)

**3D printing: slice a model with a material profile and send it to the printer**

|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner job 2026-11-14: "print that STL with PLA settings". The owner's printer takes jobs from other software only through the vendor's desktop app (Bambu Connect, Bambu Lab's official path for third-party tools). Starting a print or reading its status from outside needs the firmware's Developer Mode, which is LAN-only and disconnects the printer from the vendor cloud. So NERV prepares and hands off the job; the owner presses Print in the app. The signed-in vendor app runs on Tabgha (NERV-02, Windows 11), where NERV runs as a background service with no window: the job goes to Tabgha (F-050), and opening the app needs the owner's logged-in desktop session. |
| **Reproduce** | Ask to print an STL with a named material. |
| **Check** | The model is sliced with a named material profile (Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer, on the base that has the app); time and material are reported; the sliced file opens in Bambu Connect (`bambu-connect://import-file` link) with a checklist for the owner (printer, plate, nozzle, filament and AMS mapping, clear plate, someone nearby for the first layer); NERV never reports a print as started, because it cannot see the printer; an unknown profile is refused. Developer Mode control is out of scope unless the owner chooses it in T01. |

### <a id="b-066"></a>[🐞 B-066](#top)

**Worker-link heartbeat verification awaits nervous SQLite IPC on every frame**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🔴 Open | 🔶 P2 | 🟢 Small | 0.5 h agent + 0.25 h owner | — | — | ⏳ | — | 🤔 |

🧑 **→** Choose [how worker-link heartbeats avoid blocking on nervous SQLite IPC](decisions/worker-heartbeat-liveness.md) (B-066-T01).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | `Peer.receive` in `src/worker-link.ts` awaits `registry.bases()` and `registry.main()` on the serial `this.incoming` chain for every frame, making four `nervous` SQLite IPC calls per `worker.ping` round-trip in `serve` (`src/runtime.ts`) while `expire()` caps its wait on `this.incoming` at one `timeoutMs`. Under SQLite or IPC contention, an already-received pong stalls behind `nervous` IPC and drops the session, driving repeated timing workarounds in B-046 (PR #293, PR #361) and B-060-T02 ([PR #411](https://github.com/voidbrain/nerv/pull/411)). |
| **Reproduce** | Compare the options in [worker heartbeat liveness](decisions/worker-heartbeat-liveness.md), or run `test/worker-link.test.ts` (`B-046`) with a 150 ms heartbeat budget when `nervous` IPC latency exceeds `timeoutMs / 2`. |
| **Check** | Owner chooses Option A (in-memory registry snapshot inside `WorkerLink`, invalidated on registry changes) or Option B (decouple socket arrival liveness from the async `nervous` IPC queue); B-066-T02 implements the chosen design and adds a slow-registry regression in `test/worker-link.test.ts` (restoring a tight budget there). |

**Steps**

| Effort | Step | Estimate | Actual | Remaining | Status | Who |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|
| 🟢 Small | <a id="b-066-t01"></a>B-066-T01 — Choose how worker-link heartbeats decouple from nervous SQLite IPC | — | 0 h | 0 h agent + 0.25 h owner | Ready | [🤔](decisions/worker-heartbeat-liveness.md) |
| 🟢 Small | <a id="b-066-t02"></a>B-066-T02 — Decouple worker-link frame verification from per-frame nervous IPC | 0.5 h | 0 h | 0.5 h | Planned · waits on [B-066-T01](#b-066-t01) | ⏳ 🤖 |
| 🟢 Small | **Total** | 0.5 h (1 of 2 steps) | 0 h (0 of 2 steps recorded) | 0.5 h agent + 0.25 h owner | 0 of 2 completed | |

| **Issue** | The Gauntlet system source key is one hash over `src`, `test`, `shared`, `web`, `evals` and the evaluation tools. 100 of the 155 merges between 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-13 changed it, and each one made all seven `nerv-system-flows` cases (stress and browser included) pending again, so the ledger is stale almost all the time ([architecture reassessment](audits/2026-11-13-architecture-reassessment.md), finding 4). |
| **Reproduce** | Count merges since `1869340` whose diff touches the inputs of `systemSourceKey` in `tools/gauntlet.mjs`. |
| **Check** | A case may declare the paths it exercises; its key hashes only those plus the runner, adapter and dependency pin; a case without a declaration keeps the whole-tree key. If a scoped case misses a real regression, that case returns to the whole-tree key. |

**Bounded incident circuits instead of a global kill switch**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |

| 🔴 Open | 🔹 P3 | 🟢 Small | 1 h | — | — | 🤖 | — | — |

| **Issue** | Preserved proposal 3 of the [architecture reassessment](audits/2026-11-06-architecture-reassessment.md#3-automatic-incident-response-bounded-circuits-before-a-global-kill-switch): Spear revokes unused grants and stands down approvals by hand, but nothing detects an incident, interrupts in-flight work or responds automatically. A global automatic revocation would itself risk an outage. |
| **Reproduce** | Inject a fault (a tool repeatedly failing, a tainted input reaching an external-effect action): nothing changes until the owner spears the sortie. |
| **Check** | One circuit first, with a written trigger → response table: stop new work in the affected scope, revoke its unused grants, keep evidence, one deduplicated alert, explicit rearm. Injected faults revoke only the intended authority and keep recovery access; benign input never trips it; model suspicion is a signal for review, never authority to stop every base. |

### <a id="b-056"></a>[🐞 B-056](#top)

**A renewal the companion refuses on the Mac says it was not confirmed**

| Status | Priority | Effort | Remaining | Depends on | Unlocks | Agent | Procedures | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 🟡 Implemented | 🔹 P3 | 🟢 Small | 0.25 h owner | — | — | — | 🧑‍🔧 | — |

🧑 **→** Next: Run [part B of the companion live checks](acceptance/companion-live-checks.md#part-b) (refused renewal, English and Italian), then close B-056.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | 2026-11-12, F-015 trial: with the companion paired, the owner pasted an invitation for another runtime. `renewalInvitation` refused it on the Mac (identity mismatch), so nothing was sent and the credential was unchanged, but `pair()` shows the same text for every renewal error: *Renewal not confirmed. Inspect clients; use a new invitation to recover the pairing.* That text is for a lost reply, where the server may already have replaced the token; here it sent the owner looking for a problem that did not exist. Also seen 2026-11-12 (F-015-T03): after a failed renewal the private field keeps the previous invitation, shown only as dots, so the next paste is appended to it and fails again with the same message. |
| **Reproduce** | Pair the companion, open Renew pairing, paste an invitation from a different NERV profile (or an expired one) and choose Renew pairing. |
| **Check** | A renewal refused before any request (identity mismatch, expired credential, malformed or expired invitation) says what was wrong and that the current pairing is unchanged; only an outcome that is really unknown (no reply, Keychain save failure after the server answered) keeps the unconfirmed message; the field is empty when renewal opens again; a Swift test covers each. |

| — | <a id="b-056-t01"></a>B-056-T01 — Separate a refused renewal from an unconfirmed one in the companion | 1 h | 0 h | 0 h | Completed | 🤖 |
| 🟢 Small | **Total** | 1 h | 0 h (0 of 2 steps recorded) | 0.25 h owner | 1 of 2 completed | |
